title: Align billing with prefix/KV cache and batching semantics (token attribution rules)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

Currently our billing and rate-limiting layers attribute token usage naively as 'tokens touched by runtime' which causes two classes of correctness problems when caches and batching are involved: (1) prefix and KV cache hits sometimes cause zero model work but still get counted (or counted inconsistently across deployments), and (2) batched generation aggregates compute which makes per-request token attribution ambiguous and can lead to overcharging or double-counting on retries / fallbacks.

This ticket defines deterministic, auditable token-attribution rules and an implementation plan so that: billing, quotas, and rate limits reflect the actual model work performed (excluding prefix/KV cache reads that avoided compute), behavior is consistent across hosted/dedicated/private, and we can roll out with telemetry and rollback safety.

Scope of changes: runtime token accounting hooks, router/billing adapter changes, edge-case handling for retries/fallbacks, dashboards/alerts, and docs for supported semantics. Not in scope: wholesale redesign of pricing model or per-API pricing changes.

Why this matters:
- Customers with aggressive prefix caching (e.g., system prompt caches) expect lower bills; inconsistent meter behavior causes billing disputes.
- Batching improvements that reduce cost for the infra team must translate into customer metering benefits; otherwise value is lost.
- Rate limit enforcement must not be bypassed by cache hits in a way that causes abuse or accidental throttling mismatches.

High-level proposal (see proposed_solution for specifics):
1) Define three token types for billing: cached_prefix_tokens, cached_kv_tokens, generated_tokens. Bill only generated_tokens.
2) For batched runs, compute generated_tokens for the whole batch and deterministically attribute tokens to originating requests using generation-order attribution (first-emitted token -> request that triggered it).
3) Ensure idempotency/dedup keys are used to prevent double billing on immediate retries/fallbacks.
4) Expose per-request breakdown in usage logs and Console for auditability.
proposed_solution:
Implementation summary:

Runtime hooks:
- Add a compact event stream emitted by the serving runtime for each request/batch containing: request_id, batch_id, prefix_cache_hit_length (tokens), kv_cache_hit_length (tokens), and a generation_event sequence for the batch indicating order of new tokens and which request slot they were generated for. This must be a flat, compact JSON line logged to the billing adapter.

Billing adapter rules (deterministic algorithm):
1) For each request in a batch, billed_tokens = number of generated tokens attributed to that request according to generation_event sequence.
2) Do NOT bill prefix_cache_hit_length or kv_cache_hit_length. These are for observability only.
3) If a request is fully served from prefix cache (generated_tokens == 0), it will be billed 0 tokens but still count against per-minute request quotas (configurable policy).
4) On retries/fallbacks: use idempotency-key + original_batch_id to detect duplicate generation events within a 2-minute window; drop duplicate generated_tokens to avoid double billing.
5) For streaming responses, emit attribution events in real time; billing records are updated incrementally.

Edge cases and decisions made:
- Partial KV cache hits: treat KV-retrieved tokens as cached_kv_tokens and exclude from billing; only new decoder steps produce billed tokens.
- Non-deterministic sampling or stochastic decoders: still attribute per emitted token to a request slot using the runtime's generation_event stream (the runtime already coordinates decoding order for batches).
- Fallback to smaller model: if runtime falls back and replays the same request, use idempotency detection and attribute billed tokens to the original request only once; if different model emits additional tokens because of behavioral changes, attribute the delta but surface a reconciliation record to Billing team.

Backward compatibility:
- Old logs will still be ingestible; move to hybrid processing for 30 days to reconcile historical variance.

Rollout safety:
- Start behind feature flag; mirror billing-adapter outputs to a side datastore and compare (mirror-mode) for 2 weeks before switching live billing.

Security and privacy:
- Events emit only token counts and request identifiers (no token text). All payloads follow existing telemetry PII rules.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits generation_event streams for batched runs and includes prefix_kv counters
Billing adapter computes per-request billed_tokens per algorithm and stores them in usage ledger
Mirror mode shows <0.5% divergence between old-metering and new-metering on baseline workloads after 1 week
No customer sees >5% increase in billed tokens after rollout (goal: decrease for cache-heavy workloads)
Rate-limiter continues to enforce request-based quotas and provides configurable policy to count cache-only requests
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implement runtime hooks + telemetry tests in staging (feature-flagged)
Phase 1: enable billing-adapter mirror-mode for all traffic; collect mismatch metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 2: enable live billing for non-critical accounts and monitor invoice parity (1 week)
Phase 3: 100% rollout with alerting and 72-hour rollback window if >5% unexpected bill changes observed
Post-rollout: create migration report and update public docs/FAQ
metrics: mirror_mismatch_rate: percent of requests where new billed_tokens != old_billed_tokens
customer_cache_billing_delta: per-customer percent change in billed tokens vs baseline
duplicate_billing_events: count of idempotency-key collisions leading to duplicate charges
latency_overhead: additional p99 latency introduced by emitting generation_event stream (goal <1ms)
rate_limit_violation_delta: change in number of rejected requests after applying cache-counting policy
